title: Sandiganbayan junks Jinggoy Estrada's appeal vs. 90-day suspension
summary: The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division has junked the motion for reconsideration filed by the camp of Senator Jinggoy Estrada challenging the second 90-day preventive suspension issued against him in…

blocks.text: The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division has junked the motion for reconsideration filed by the camp of Senator Jinggoy Estrada challenging the second 90-day preventive suspension issued against him in connection with the flood control anomaly.

In a resolution penned by Associate Justice Zaldy Trespeses, the anti-graft court noted that the preventive suspension issued by the Second Division in June 2026 is different from what the Fifth Division issued in October 2026.

"The cases pending in this division are distinct and independent from that pending in the Second Division. Any perceived gap in the court's imposition of preventive suspension in these cases is simply a result of the independent functioning of the Sandiganbayan's division," the resolution read.

Cited in the resolution, Estrada argued that he has already served his 90-day preventive suspension as imposed by the anti-graft court's Second Division. He also argued that his suspension had him "prevented from performing and exercising his duties and responsibilities as a Senator."
The senator also argued that another 90 days of preventive suspension would suspend him for a total of 180 days, "which would convert a preventive measure into a penal sanction."
But the Sandiganbayan's Fifth Division said that the suspensions issued against Estrada would not make him inactive indefinitely.

"The imposition of the suspension here is a ministerial duty of the court to impose upon an accused in fulfillment of the statutes under which he is presently being charged with," the resolution read.

The Fifth Division in September also affirmed its decision in July denying Estrada’s motion to fix bail in the P573-million plunder case he is facing over his alleged involvement in the flood control mess, citing lack of merit.
Meanwhile, the Office of the Ombudsman backed the anti-graft court's ruling.

"The resolution sustains the position of the prosecution that the cases before the Fifth Division are separate and independent from the graft case pending before the Second Division, in which Senator Estrada had previously served a 90-day preventive suspension," said Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano in a statement.

"We maintain that the imposition of preventive suspension is a procedural safeguard intended to preserve the integrity of judicial proceedings and does not constitute a determination of guilt," he added. —AOL, GMA News
